title: Soyuz-MS

sources.title: JoyPro cockpit catalog (panels, items and grip functions of the variant)

intro: Soyuz-MS is the current version of the Soyuz, flying to the International Space Station since 2016. It has the digital Neptun-ME panel and the Kurs-NA automatic docking system. The hand controllers are taken as unchanged from the Soyuz-TM, so this guide builds on the Soyuz-TM guide.

panels.name: Neptun-ME digital panel
panels.text: The glass panel in front of the commander, introduced with the Soyuz TMA-M.
panels.context: It replaced the older panel with two screens and command keys.

controls.name: Two displays
controls.text: Two screens that show the systems and the approach to the space station.
controls.context: The commander watches the automatic docking on them and takes over if needed.

controls.name: Command keys
controls.text: Keys next to the screens that send commands; the crew still reaches them with a pointer stick.
controls.context: Strapped into the seats, the crew cannot reach the panel with their hands. JoyPro's sources do not describe its single switches.

panels.name: Crew seats
panels.text: The three body-shaped seats of the descent capsule.
panels.context: Each seat is shaped to its astronaut's body for launch and landing.

controls.name: Commander's seat
controls.text: The middle seat, in front of the panel and between the two hand controllers.
controls.context: The commander flies from here when a manual approach is needed.

controls.name: Side seats
controls.text: The seats of the flight engineer and the third crew member, left and right of the commander.
controls.context: The flight engineer on the left helps the commander with the systems.
